correctness.rationale: Definition uses complements of disconnected 3-sets (not independent triples). An independent implementation checked all four complete ordered facet-complement files at n=17,18,19,20 against all disconnected triples (408,528,665,820 facets), verified every preceding-facet ridge-containment shelling intersection, and counted spanning facets 1,10,20,31. All four orders passed with no missing/duplicate facets. Independently enumerated each Alexander dual at n=11..16 and computed exact F2 reduced homology (K nonzero q/r = (5,1),(3,6),(3,40),(3,15),(3,1),(2,3)); duality places these strictly below top dimension n-4 and obstructs pure shellability. n<=10 is void because each vertex has at most one nonneighbor. For n>=21, Theorem 1.4 of Chauhan--Shukla arXiv:2603.23155 yields shellability and wedge counts; no false infinite extrapolation from the four certificates.

value.rationale: Closes all four exact missing boundary orders of the published sharp n=4p+1 shellability conjecture for fixed p=4. Each certificate is a constructive exhaustive shelling order; together with established large-n theorem and low-n obstructions it settles a genuinely motivated infinite threshold and exact wedge formula. The tabulated small-n Betti ranks are acknowledged prior, not presented as novel.

final_claim: For n>=11, ordinary three-cut Delta_3(C_n^4) shellable iff n>=17; for n>=17 it is wedge^(binom(n-8,2)-35) of S^(n-4).
limitations: Fixed fourth power p=4, ordinary three-cut only, n>=11 nonvoid; no all-p shellability theorem.
Low-range obstruction is over F2, sufficient for failure of shellability but not a full integral homotopy computation.
